To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the amyloid β (Aß) depositions in the brain are composed of different Aß variants, and that the composition varies depending on the pathological subgroup of Aß‐related diseases.
we identified a new Aβ variant, Aβ1‐x, which is present in the brain of AD and CAA patients, and which is a major Aβ variant in CAA.

1) CAA is a distinct disease with a different molecular composition of Aβ than plaques, 2) the CAA‐specific Aβ species are modified by glycosylation and phosphorylation, 3) these modified Aβ species are present in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) of patients with CAA and 4) modified Aβ species in the CSF of CAA patients are potential biomarkers of vascular pathology.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular composition of Aβ deposits in plaques and vessels of AD, and with its relation to the pathogenic mechanisms of Aβ deposition.
the molecular composition of Aβ deposits and its relation to disease progression.
the characterization of the molecular composition of Aβ in AD and other dementias, with a particular focus on vascular amyloid.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Aβ variants in AD are not identical in plaques and CAA.
the amyloid variants in the different pathological subgroups of AD are not identical.
CAA is a distinct entity, but it is not clear if it is a distinct disease entity, or a distinct disease process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a novel Aβ variant (Aβ‐N3pE) in AD‐related brain regions, which is associated with the early stages of Aβ plaque formation, and is a major component of CAA.
the amyloid β (A β) depositions in the brain of Alzheimer's disease are composed of different variants of A β peptides that have been modified by different enzymes.
we identified distinct amyloid variants in plaques and in vascular deposits of CAA.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amyloid deposits in the brain of patients with CAA are composed of modified Aβ variants, and the molecular composition of the amyloid deposits is distinct in CAA compared to AD.
the composition of Aβ deposits is different between plaques and CAA, and this is reflected by a different pattern of post‐translational modifications.
the molecular composition of Aβ deposits in plaques and vessels differs between AD and other β‐amyloid diseases, and that the molecular profile of vascular Aβ may reflect the underlying pathology.
